title: Rolling Capacity Allocator: epoch windows & microburst scenarios (NA / EU / APAC)
content:
Purpose:
This working sheet lays out a rolling-capacity allocation approach ("epoch windows") for NA / EU / APAC to handle predictable growth and short-duration microbursts without overprovisioning. Focus is on: warm-pool sizing, epoch activation cadence, latency SLO mapping, and mitigation steps when activation misses target.

Context / constraints (short notes):
- Business: Q3 product launches + two enterprise pilot customers expected to add sustained throughput in NA and EU.
- Hardware mix considered: H100 (prod-high), A100-80GB (prod), L4 (cost-sensitive burst tiers).
- Target utilization bands: baseline 60–70% (cost-opt), steady-state 70–85% (SLA), avoid 90%+ sustained.
- Warm pools must support 3–8 minute activation for heavy context loads (KV warm start).
- Cross-region fallback allowed for <12% traffic by policy; >12% requires soft-fallback plus throttling.

High-level recommendation (summary):
- Move from monthly tranche activations to overlapping 10-day epoch windows per region. Each epoch tuned to account for forecast variance and one microburst cushion.
- Maintain warm-pool capacity equal to 6%–9% of regional active fleet for H100/A100; 12% for L4.
- Reserve a 2-epoch emergency buffer (cold reserve) per region to cover runway errors (roughly 5% capacity).

Epoch window model (how it works):
- Epoch length = 10 days.
- Overlap = 4 days between consecutive epochs (ensures continuous activation ramp).
- Decision point: Day 6 of epoch -> telemetry cut (utilization, queue length, tail-latency).
- If telemetry > threshold -> trigger immediate 24–48h accelerated activation within same epoch.

Regional forecast table (concise, numbers are planned GPU equivalents in effective H100 units) :

Region | Baseline (Jun 2026) | Forecast +3mo (Sep 2026) | Forecast +6mo (Dec 2026) | Warm-pool target (pct) | Emergency buffer (pct)
NA     | 120 H100 eq         | 165 H100 eq               | 210 H100 eq               | 8%                    | 5%
EU     | 85 H100 eq          | 110 H100 eq               | 140 H100 eq               | 7%                    | 5%
APAC   | 40 H100 eq          | 62 H100 eq                | 88 H100 eq                | 9%                    | 6%

Notes on numbers: conversions assume H100 baseline; A100 counted as 0.85 H100-eq; L4 counted as 0.15 H100-eq for burst routing.

Microburst scenarios (examples and mitigation):
1) Marketing flash (NA): +160% request spike for 45 minutes during weekday morning peak.
   - Expected effect: queueing on prod tier, tail-latency increase ~2.6x, auto-scaler may react too slowly (startup + cold-kv penalty).
   - Mitigation: pre-warm policy if predicted (via traffic signal) or immediate shift of 10% of L4 capacity to handle short synchronous requests via fast-path. Canary rule: if spike >100% and duration <2h, prioritize latency-sensitive routes to warm pool.

2) Model rollout quality regression causes replays in EU (customer debug load): +40% sustained for 18 hours.
   - Mitigation: auto-rollout pause + route degraded traffic to lower-cost A100 pool and enable grace-throughput throttling for non-critical endpoints.

3) APAC partner load (unexpected): +300% for 20 minutes with high context lengths (large KV).
   - Mitigation: immediate cross-region soft-fallback to NA up to 10%, enable p99-latency-aware shedding for the remainder, trigger 2-epoch emergency buffer activation if exceed threshold.

Activation cadence & timeline (example Q3 sprint plan):
- Weekly planning cadence: Mon (epoch start), Fri (visibility sync).
- Epoch activation heatmap (sample 6-week window):
  Week 1: NA epoch A active; EU epoch X pre-warm; APAC epoch 1 monitor
  Week 2: NA epoch A overlap -> B ramp; EU X active; APAC 1 -> 2 overlap
  Week 3: NA B active; EU Y start; APAC 2 active; (evaluate telemetry on day6 of each epoch)
  Week 4: corrective activations where telemetry > thresholds (24–48h fast lane)
  Week 5: scheduled tranche for enterprise pilot (NA) -> permanent commit review
  Week 6: re-evaluate warm-pool percentages based on observed microburst behaviour

Telemetry thresholds (decision triggers):
- Avg utilization > 82% for 6h -> pre-emptive epoch accelerate
- Queue length percentile (99th) > 85ms for 15m -> add warm-pool target +2%
- Cold start rate > 4% of requests over 30m -> increase pre-warm for next epoch by 3%

Operational playbook (short checklist):
- Day 0 (pre-epoch): confirm capacity tickets, cloud onboarding/quotas in place, vendor ETA for new racks.
- Day 4: jitter test (fire synthetic microburst test for 10m at 2x baseline) and validate warm-pool activation time.
- Day 6: first telemetry cut -> decide accelerate / normal / scale-down.
- Day 8: runway check -> ensure emergency buffer remains available.
- Day 10: roll epoch metrics to planner; update forecasts and notes for next epoch.

SLA mapping & customer impact notes:
- For enterprise clients with 99.9% latency SLA: route to H100 prod pool only; if H100 oversubbed, promote dedicated capacity or throttle lower-priority endpoints.
- For self-serve users: allow fallthrough to A100/L4 paths with reduced context budgets and longer p99 target.

Outstanding questions / open decisions:
- Should warm-pool be charged to product budget or infra (long-term accounting)? (asked to Finance: J. Ortega)
- Can SRE team accept 4-day overlap operations given on-call bandwidth? Need signoff from SRE lead (Jon Park).
- Are we comfortable with 10-day epochs vs 7-day? Shorter epochs reduce risk but increase churn and provisioning cost. Running a 30-day A/B in July recommended.

Action items (owners & due dates):
- Implement synthetic jitter test harness for epoch validation (owner: Rajat, due: 2026-07-16)
- Add cold-start telemetry dashboard card to Console "Epoch activations" (owner: Maya, due: 2026-07-09)
- Finance review on warm-pool chargeback model (owner: Lena, due: 2026-07-20)
- Pilot overlapping epoch model in NA for 6 weeks starting 2026-07-26 (owner: Carmen, due: plan by 2026-07-12)

Notes to self / quick logs:
- Ran quick sim: 8% warm-pool in NA reduced p99 tail during 2x microburst by ~35% in latency but increased cost by ~1.9% (rough calc).
- APAC cold start penalty higher for KV-heavy prompts; consider region-specific warmup script for KV restore.

References and links:
- Fleet allocator repo (design doc link in linked_artifacts), existing quota playbook, and SLO runbook.

End of sheet.

(If this is useful, we can convert to a tracking sheet with columns for epoch id, start/end, allocated H100-eq, actual peak utilization, actions taken, and cost delta.)
